findings.obs_text: Where suppose opens a case, the qualifiers are the numbers of the case and the answers to it: five short of fifty, forty, thirty, twenty, ten in Gen 18:28 to Gen 18:32, with there and again; the negators reach the Lord's answer (I will not destroy) and Abraham's plea that the Lord not be angry, not the supposing. In Eze 18:14 the negator reaches the son's not doing as his father did.

A negator reaches the supposing itself in 2Sa 13:32, 2Sa 13:33 and Jam 1:7: let not my lord suppose, must not suppose; the view is forbidden. In Act 2:15 and Act 13:25 the negator reaches what the view gets wrong (not drunk, I am not he), and in Act 17:29 the negator reaches the thinking that the divine being is like an image of human imagination.

In 1Cor 8:2 not and yet reach the knowing that the one who imagines lacks; in Jam 4:5 to no purpose is what the readers are asked whether they suppose of the Scripture; in Luk 7:43 larger names the debt in Simon's view and rightly is Jesus' verdict on it.

Where supposing is a belief an act rests on, the qualifiers describe the act or its setting, not the supposing: relatives and acquaintances where they search in Luk 2:44, quickly and there in Joh 11:31, where in Joh 20:15, woke in Act 16:27, along the shore in Act 27:13; in Joh 21:25 many other things are what the writer supposes the world could not hold, and in Pro 18:11 rich names the man whose wealth is a wall in his imagination.

older.finding: Righteous is here the godly, the righteous, the upright, the wicked or the ungodly as a class of persons toward whom an act is directed or whom an event befalls (the Lord keeps the godly, do not envy the wicked, Christ died for the ungodly); the act is named by another word of the verse.
older.reason: it states a face or use of the righteous words; the righteous collection owns it
